purpose: Per-file named causes for corpus files that are NOT passing. Exists to remove the ~35min triage phase that every wave-2 agent paid independently and then threw away. A brief MUST draw its worklist from here rather than asking an agent to re-triage. Entries are what the agent that filed them measured; a stale entry is a bug -- re-derive before budgeting.
provenance: wave-2 agents w2/agent-1 (tls), w2/agent-2 (http), w2/agent-3 (fs), round 10; tls per-file causes extracted from the r10-j6 full run logs at integration (155 non-pass tls/https: 119 fail, 19 timeout, 17 self-skip)
how_to_use: Group by `cause`, count files per cause, budget mechanisms x 10min + 55min overhead. Do NOT budget by subsystem -- see compat/README.md 'Allocate agents by cause family, not by subsystem'.
caveat: Coverage is uneven: the fs inventory is per-file and complete (58 files); tls and http are recorded at cause-shape granularity because that is the level their agents reported. Filling the tls/http per-file rows is itself a cheap, high-leverage task.

platform-impossible.note: macOS-only, Windows-only, or needs JSC Temporal. Already classified `skipped`. NOT reachable -- exclude from every target.

filehandle-lock-ref-protocol.note: kLocked/kCloseSync/kClosePromise absent; fh.pull/pullSync/writer missing; no close-error propagation ('Missing expected rejection'). ~570 lines of node's fs.promises.ts.
filehandle-lock-ref-protocol.action: densest single remaining fs mechanism -- one dedicated round

fs-watch.note: 3 are hangs: a watcher registers as a pollable but holds no fd, so the drain's stall clock never advances. Also err.path missing on ENOENT, symlink loop, and BigIntStats carrying 4 Date props node's zero-row omits.

realpath-js-resolver.note: mbun uses weakly_canonical; node uses a non-native JS resolver with its own cache semantics.

fs-not-routed-through-internalBinding.note: internalBinding('fs') EXISTS but mbun's fs does not call through it, so tests that monkey-patch binding.readdir / binding.writeFileUtf8 (and count exactly 2 calls) see nothing.
fs-not-routed-through-internalBinding.action: architectural: routing fs through the binding is a prerequisite for any test that patches it

node-test-subtest-failures.note: node:test based; failure is inside a subtest. flush pair needs validateBoolean(options.flush) + a real fsyncSync visible to t.mock.method. test-fs-glob alone is 243/448 subtests failing -- a glob round of its own.
node-test-subtest-failures.action: split: the flush pair is cheap, glob is not

fs-one-off.action: each is 1 file; only worth batching, never worth a dedicated agent

http-timeout-shape-A-server-outlives-dea.signature: Server{listening} + zero sockets; server.close() sits in a client callback that never fired
http-timeout-shape-A-server-outlives-dea.note: NOT an event-loop bug. The client flow died; node would also hold the loop here. Fix the client-side flow, not the loop.
http-timeout-shape-A-server-outlives-dea.action: one mechanism, highest file count in http

http-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.signature: Server{listening} + live socket pair, _wq=0, no ref'd timer

http-timeout-shape-D-actually-a-native-c.signature: no hang dump at all; native WTFCrashWithInfo
http-timeout-shape-D-actually-a-native-c.note: MISFILED as timeout -- these are crashes. Any 'sweep the hangs' brief that includes them is budgeting the wrong work.

tls-pkcs12.note: CORRECTED LEAD: briefed as an OpenSSL legacy-provider search-path fix. Reality: only a no-op `loadPKCS12() {}` stub exists and there is no d2i_PKCS12 call anywhere. The work is 'write PKCS#12 parsing, then load the provider'.
tls-pkcs12.action: do NOT budget as a config fix; grep d2i_PKCS12 first

tls-version-and-ciphersuites.note: CORRECTED LEAD: briefed as '@SECLEVEL=0 is never forwarded'. It IS forwarded, to SSL_CTX_set_cipher_list. Remaining gap is narrower: SSL_CTX_set_ciphersuites (TLS 1.3 suites use a different setter) plus --tls-min-v1.x last-flag-wins.
tls-version-and-ciphersuites.action: re-derive the file count from the narrower gap before budgeting

tls-verify-error-code-mapping.cause: mbun surfaces OpenSSL verify code 20 (UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY, 'issuer not found locally') where node surfaces 21 (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE, 'chain has one non-self-signed cert'). One file surfaces null instead of any code. The two codes differ by how a one-cert chain is treated, so this is chain-depth / X509_STORE flag handling, not a trust-store contents problem.
tls-verify-error-code-mapping.confidence: CAUSE named -- the actual/expected pair identifies it uniquely
tls-verify-error-code-mapping.action: single mechanism; highest-value tls cluster found so far

tls-connect-duplex-transport-unimplement.cause: mbun throws its own explicit error: 'tls.connect (Duplex socket transport) requires the socket event loop + real SSL_CTX handshake (DEFERRED)'. tls.connect over a caller-supplied Duplex/`socket:` option is simply not implemented.
tls-connect-duplex-transport-unimplement.confidence: CAUSE named -- mbun says so itself
tls-connect-duplex-transport-unimplement.action: architectural; a known-unimplemented path, not a bug hunt

tls-protocol-method-validation.cause: SSLv2_method/SSLv3_method and friends must be rejected with ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_METHOD.

tls-mustcall-never-fired.cause: node's common.mustCall reports 'Expected exactly N, actual 0' at exit: an expected event never fired. SAME CLASS as http-timeout-shape-A (a dead flow), but here the process exits rather than hanging. The specific missing event differs per file and must be read from the log's stack (e.g. test-https-agent-keylog wants a 'keylog' event 10x).
tls-mustcall-never-fired.confidence: CLASS named, per-file event NOT yet named
tls-mustcall-never-fired.action: read the named event out of each log before budgeting

tls-value-divergence-UNSPLIT.cause: NOT A CAUSE -- this is the residue of the 'strictly equal' bucket whose actual/expected pair is a bare number or boolean (`5 !== 3`, `false !== true`), which identifies nothing on its own. Recorded as explicitly unsplit so nobody mistakes it for a mechanism. Calling a manifestation a cause has cost this project three separate rounds.
tls-value-divergence-UNSPLIT.confidence: MANIFESTATION ONLY -- do not budget as one family
tls-value-divergence-UNSPLIT.action: split per file by reading the assertion's surrounding test intent; do not hand this bucket to an agent whole

clusters.handshake-alert-failure (5): first error is `ssl: error:...:SSL routines::sslv3 alert handshake failure`
clusters.no-cipher-match (2): first error is `Error: No cipher match`

tls-small-clusters.confidence: each pair/triple is a plausible single mechanism; unverified

tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.signature: Uniform across all 12: NET.pending=0, handles=3, items=3 -- one listening Server plus the client/server socket pair, and BOTH sockets readable=true writable=true destroyed=false _paused=false _wq=0. Nothing queued, nothing paused, both ends open and idle.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.cause: A genuinely stalled exchange: each side is waiting for bytes the other will never send. NOT an event-loop bug -- node would hold the loop here identically. This is the fifth independent confirmation that hangs in this project are protocol-semantics gaps rather than handle-lifetime bugs.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.hypothesis_i_checked_and_REFUTED: I read NET.pending=0 as 'no fd is in the poll set, so arriving bytes never wake the loop', which would have made all 12 one bug. js_net.cppm:138 says pending counts bounded in-flight operations (e.g. a fetch awaiting its response), NOT poll-set membership. What holds the loop is _held/_loopOpen, both true here. pending=0 is normal. Do not brief an agent on the poll-set theory.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.confidence: CLASS named and uniform; NOT a single mechanism
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.action: largest tls block. Budget per file or per small group, not as one sweep -- and note it is dominated by abort/destroy/attach-timing cases, which suggests the shared theme is teardown DURING handshake rather than steady-state transfer

tls-timeout-shape-A-dead-client-flow.cause: Client flow died; server.close() sits in a callback that never fired. Same shape as http-timeout-shape-A (10 files) -- fix the client flow, not the loop.
tls-timeout-shape-A-dead-client-flow.action: share a mechanism with the http shape-A block; consider one agent for both (15 files total)

tls-timeout-shape-D-native-block.signature: hang_dump.js produces NO dump at all (rc=124) even with a ref'd timer bounding the pump's poll park
tls-timeout-shape-D-native-block.cause: The pump is blocked inside native code and JS never regains control. Most severe shape: a JS-level fix cannot reach it.
tls-timeout-shape-D-native-block.confidence: CLASS named, native frame NOT yet identified
tls-timeout-shape-D-native-block.action: attach gdb or use modules/crash_handler; identify the blocking native call before budgeting

coverage_note: tls timeouts are now triaged: 19 files -> 3 shapes (B:12, A:5, D:2), collapsed by running tools/integration/hang_dump.js over every one. This is the same collapse the http block underwent, and it reproduces the same headline: none of the 19 is an event-loop bug. Cost ~5 minutes total, which is the argument for triaging centrally rather than making each agent pay for it.
